scope: 14 pointwise APIs beyond Asin; CPU only. Full remains default; required GPU continues to reject these new operations.
fixture: Random valid-domain closes in [0.125,0.875), 10000 and 100000 bars; 8-worker budget; Full and LatestOnly builders.
native: TALib.NETCore 0.5.0 serial public functions and our AiDotNet parallel wrapper. Final native arrays are uninitialized, like ours; before-presence native arrays were zero-initialized.
result: No statistically clear win over the fastest tested native arm at either size. Warm all-defined LatestOnly allocation falls from about 1567 KiB to about 786 KiB at 100k.
ownership: Read-only all-one presence arrays share one exact-length cache entry, capped at 8 MiB retained. Cache replacement never mutates prior arrays. Undefined-domain outputs materialize owned double presence arrays before BuildAsync returns; pooled bitmaps never escape.
limits: Warm benchmark excludes initial presence-cache allocation; mixed sizes can miss the single-entry cache.
Domain bitmaps retain pooled capacity; at 100k this is about 16 KiB.
Full retains all original bars and still trails native values-only output.
Serial and up-to-eight-worker native routes were tested; no blanket fastest-native or GPU win is claimed.
The remaining shared catalog is tracked separately; historical normalized-adapter evidence is not promoted to current native qualification.
tensors_source_review: Double SqrtOperator and FloorOperator vector overloads currently unpack lanes and call scalar Math methods; changing to those APIs alone would not provide a faster SIMD kernel.
